item.title: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra produces a proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture
item.description: GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra has generated a proof for the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture, a longstanding problem in graph theory. The proof was published in a PDF document made publicly available in July 2026. This development marks a significant milestone in the application of advanced AI models to complex mathematical problems.

item.title: Apple sues OpenAI and former employees for alleged trade secret theft involving unreleased technologies [ ! ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI and former Apple employees, accusing them of stealing trade secrets related to unreleased technologies and confidential information. The lawsuit names Chang Liu and Tang Tan, former Apple engineers now at OpenAI, and alleges that OpenAI's hardware efforts led by Jony Ive involve misappropriated Apple intellectual property. The complaint details that Tan used insider knowledge during job interviews to extract further confidential information from Apple employees, including directing candidates to bring actual Apple hardware components to interviews. Apple claims it raised concerns with OpenAI in February 2026, but the company did not respond, and the lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California to stop the alleged misconduct.

item.title: Meta removes Instagram AI image generation feature after global user backlash over automatic opt-in [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Meta has disabled its Muse Image AI feature on Instagram following widespread criticism over its automatic activation for millions of users without explicit consent. The feature allowed public Instagram posts to be used for AI-generated images, sparking concerns about privacy and ethical use of personal content. The backlash included criticism from online experts and industry groups who argued that opting out rather than opting in was unethical and that users were not adequately informed. Meta had planned to expand the feature to Facebook, Messenger, and WhatsApp but reversed course after negative media coverage and public outcry.

item.title: Report: Big Tech doubles debt to $350 billion amid AI investment surge
item.description: Big technology companies have doubled their debt load to $350 billion as they increase spending on artificial intelligence projects. This surge in borrowing reflects the sector's aggressive investment in AI development and infrastructure. The increased debt is driven by major firms seeking to expand their AI capabilities and maintain competitive advantage in the rapidly evolving technology landscape. The financial strategy highlights the high stakes and significant capital requirements associated with AI innovation.

item.title: Millfolio details local AI tagging system for managing transaction data on Mac M2 with 16GB RAM, optimizing batch processing and resource use [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Millfolio describes a local AI infrastructure approach for managing financial transaction data on a Mac M2 with 16GB RAM, focusing on efficient batch processing to keep the laptop responsive. The system uses a combination of string, reference, and AI-generated tags to classify transactions once and store results for fast querying without repeated model inference. The tagging process involves running AI classification in batches with a disk-backed queue that prioritizes background work to avoid interfering with interactive use. Duplicate transaction descriptions are collapsed to reduce inference calls, and the system supports adjustable processing priorities to balance speed and resource consumption. This approach enables scalable local AI use despite hardware constraints by precomputing costly AI tags and relying on fast string matching at query time.

item.title: Analysis of AI limitations and social divisions highlights risks of job loss, misinformation, and polarized views on AI's role and capabilities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The article examines the polarized perspectives on artificial intelligence, ranging from fears of job displacement and AI consciousness to outright rejection of AI technologies. It emphasizes that large language models (LLMs) operate by predicting probable text patterns without true understanding, which can lead to errors and misleading outputs. The discussion references philosophical thought experiments and recent research to illustrate the gap between AI's apparent intelligence and actual comprehension. It warns that societal divisions fueled by extreme views on AI could have significant social impacts, underscoring the need to coexist with AI while recognizing its current limitations and potential risks.

item.title: Researchers propose Context Graphs for proactive enterprise AI agents that deliver actionable insights before queries, demonstrating faster and more precise information delivery in contract, incident, and sales scenarios [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A new enterprise AI approach introduces proactive agents that provide relevant, actionable information to workers before they ask. The method uses a Context Graph, a dynamic relational data structure modeling enterprise entities and their evolving states, combined with a Delta Detection Engine to monitor changes, a Proactivity Scorer to rank insights, and a Surfacing Layer powered by a large language model to present notifications with explanations. Implemented in Python with NetworkX and the Anthropic Claude API, the system was evaluated in contract lifecycle management, engineering incident response, and sales pipeline hygiene, achieving high precision and reducing information delivery time from 47 minutes to under 30 seconds compared to reactive baselines.

item.title: Researchers develop AI tool integrating economic and biophysical models to assess agricultural supply chain disruptions via natural language queries [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have created an AI-powered tool that combines economic models (GTAP) with biophysical models (APSIM) to analyze disruptions in agricultural supply chains. This integration enables policymakers and market participants to evaluate cross-disciplinary impacts by interacting with the system through natural language queries and responses, improving understanding of supply chain resilience.

item.title: Researchers propose adversarial social epistemology framework to analyze trust and information distortion in human and large language model communication networks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The paper introduces an adversarial social epistemology framework to study complex communication environments where public assertions depend on chains of testimony, inference, and institutional trust. It addresses how agents may manipulate information for private or reputational gains, a phenomenon not fully explained by existing concepts like epistemic bubbles or misinformation diffusion. The authors develop analytical tools and mechanisms to detect and address breaches of trust by auditing the inferential chains that support public communications.

item.title: Survey examines large language models for medical reasoning, linking clinical competencies with computational methods and evaluating 18 models across five reasoning levels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent survey analyzes the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) in healthcare, focusing on their application in medical reasoning and patient care. It introduces a framework connecting clinical competencies, based on Miller's Pyramid, with computational reasoning patterns and evaluates 18 advanced models using a benchmark dataset spanning five levels of medical reasoning. The study finds that specialist medical models perform better in diagnosis tasks, while general models excel in decision support and dialogue. It also discusses challenges such as data limitations, hallucinations, and grounding, and suggests directions for developing safer, more reliable AI systems for clinical workflows.

item.title: Researchers propose alignment plausibility framework to assure safety of large language models in mental health support by embedding clinical values and oversight [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new framework called alignment plausibility has been proposed to improve the safety of large language models (LLMs) used in mental health support by mirroring clinical practice safety standards. It involves explicitly defining values based on clinical norms, embedding these values during model training, and implementing oversight mechanisms to detect drift and prevent long-term harm during deployment. This approach aims to provide regulators and developers with a structured method to assess and ensure AI systems align with positive health outcomes while minimizing risks such as dependency or misinformation.

item.title: Researchers introduce idiobionics to address privacy risks in intelligent robotic prostheses amid potential adversarial attacks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A new research field called idiobionics has been proposed to explore privacy challenges in intelligent robotic prostheses, or bionic limbs, which use advanced sensors and AI for semiautonomous control. These devices enhance user functionality but also create vulnerabilities that malicious actors could exploit to compromise user privacy. The paper defines idiobionics, reviews related work, presents preliminary evidence of possible adversarial attacks on these prostheses, and outlines open research questions to mitigate privacy risks and encourage adoption. The study aims to support the safe integration of advanced bionic limbs into daily life by addressing privacy concerns inherent in their design and operation.

item.title: Infinity-Parser2 releases two multimodal document parsing models with a 5-million-sample bilingual dataset and multi-task reinforcement learning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Infinity-Parser2 is a large multimodal model designed for end-to-end document parsing, addressing the scarcity of annotated parsing datasets by using a scalable data synthesis engine to create a 5-million-sample bilingual corpus with diverse document types and detailed annotations. The model employs multi-task reinforcement learning with eight co-trained objectives that integrate perception, structure, and reasoning. Two variants are released: Infinity-Parser2-Flash, optimized for faster inference, and Infinity-Parser2-Pro, focused on precision, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks and generalizes well across various document parsing tasks.

item.title: VectorizationLLM: Google-based AI assistant for MATLAB vectorization and analysis education at NYIT [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: VectorizationLLM is a Large Language Model derived from Google's open-weight LLMs, designed to assist students in learning topics such as smart vectorization, time/wave vector analysis, piecewise functions, Fourier analysis, and differential equations using MATLAB. It supports the Applied Computational Analysis II course at New York Institute of Technology Old Westbury's Electrical & Computer Engineering Technology department by providing detailed explanations and examples from class notes without directly answering questions. The model uses a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) knowledge base and system prompt architecture to generate responses that include code, text, and images, aiming to serve as an instructive assistant rather than a direct answer provider.

item.title: Researchers develop graph neural network model for real-time hand gesture recognition using sEMG signals with 99% accuracy and 48ms processing time on M1 Pro CPU [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have created a machine learning method that uses graph neural networks to recognize hand gestures in real time from surface electromyography (sEMG) signals collected via an 8-electrode MyoBand device on the forearm. Tested on data from eight healthy subjects, the model represents muscle activation patterns as graphs and achieves an average classification accuracy of 99% with a processing time of 48 milliseconds on an M1 Pro CPU, outperforming existing techniques. This approach is suitable for applications such as advanced prosthetic control and augmented reality, where accurate and immediate gesture recognition is critical.

item.title: Study compares single LLM, retrieval-augmented, and multi-agent AI systems for straight-through underwriting of small commercial policies, finding multi-agent approach improves transparency and accuracy [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A recent study evaluates three AI architectures-single large language model, basic retrieval-augmented generation, and a multi-agent agentic system-for straight-through underwriting of small commercial Business Owner Policies. The research finds that the multi-agent system, which integrates targeted data retrieval, external verification, and multi-step rule evaluation, outperforms the others, especially in complex cases with missing information, by enhancing transparency, auditability, and supporting human oversight. The study uses a synthetic but realistic experimental environment to compare the underwriting pipelines, highlighting the benefits of structured retrieval and reflection in avoiding unsupported decisions. This work illustrates how emerging AI architectures can address actuarial priorities such as regulated decision workflows and human-in-the-loop governance in insurance underwriting.

item.title: Researchers propose Feedback Manipulation Regularization to improve offline imitation learning agent alignment using evaluative feedback in sequential decision tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduced Feedback Manipulation Regularization (FMR), a method that integrates evaluative feedback as a corrective signal during offline imitation learning to better align agents with human values. Unlike prior multi-stage approaches, FMR operates in a single stage and is algorithm-agnostic, targeting fully sequential decision-making environments. The method was evaluated in adapted Safety Gymnasium environments, showing up to a 98% reduction in misalignment across various imitation learning algorithms. FMR demonstrated robustness even with limited or noisy demonstration data, suggesting its potential for improving policy alignment in offline training scenarios.

item.title: Researchers release Nigeria Machinery Usage and Failures Dataset with 89 records and introduce a domain-grounded chain-of-thought reasoning method for sparse numeric data [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have published the Nigeria Machinery Usage and Failures Dataset, containing 89 machine-level records across 28 indicators from Nigeria's manufacturing and oil and gas sectors spanning 2006 to 2025. Alongside the dataset, they developed a method to create chain-of-thought reasoning examples from sparse numeric data, resulting in 94 prompt-completion-reasoning trace entries that are fully domain-grounded and aligned with real-world data. The dataset and reasoning materials are publicly available under a CC-BY-4.0 license and intended as a reference and seed resource rather than a large-scale training set due to limited observations.

item.title: Researchers map and control large language model personalities using OCEAN traits with low-rank adapters, showing monotonic, additive effects and links to safety behaviors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent study introduces a method to characterize and manipulate large language model personas by mapping them onto a behavioral trait space based on the OCEAN framework: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism. Researchers trained low-rank adapters to adjust these traits across six models from three families, finding that trait changes are largely monotonic and additive, allowing for mixed personas without degrading model capabilities. The study also reveals that certain trait adjustments influence safety-related behaviors such as frustration and sycophancy. Additionally, the team developed an unsupervised psychometric pipeline to identify behavioral factors from model outputs, linking personality control with model editing and safety considerations.

item.title: Researchers evaluate LSTM and GRU models for classifying autism-related self-stimulatory hand behaviors from video, finding peak accuracy near 98% at 15-frame sampling intervals [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study tested sequence-based neural networks, specifically LSTM and GRU architectures, on pose-derived features from a behavioral dataset to detect autism-related self-stimulatory hand movements. Both models outperformed previous CNN approaches, achieving peak accuracies of 97.5% and 98.75% respectively at a frame sampling interval of every 15 frames. The research also assessed ten data augmentation techniques within a transfer learning framework, identifying horizontal flipping as the most effective standalone method and highlighting the importance of upsampling for maintaining performance. Additionally, a personalized machine learning approach training models on individual subjects' video segments produced consistent predictions. These findings provide guidance on model architecture, temporal sampling, and augmentation strategies for video-based behavioral classification in clinical settings with limited data.

item.title: Researchers introduce AgentNAS, combining large language models and neural architecture search to design modular neural networks, achieving state-of-the-art results on 11 of 17 tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed AgentNAS, a method that uses large language models (LLMs) to generate initial neural network architectures which are then converted into modular scaffolds for neural architecture search (NAS) to optimize without manual input. Tested on 17 diverse tasks including classification and segmentation, AgentNAS outperformed existing expert-designed models on 11 tasks, demonstrating the complementary strengths of LLM-driven design and NAS refinement. The approach was validated across three different LLMs, confirming its robustness, and the code has been made publicly available.

item.title: Researchers propose Concretized Proposition Prompting to resolve composition-knowledge tradeoff in large language models, improving reasoning on medical and math benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Concretized Proposition Prompting (CPP), a framework designed to address the challenge large language models face in balancing compositionality and knowledgeability, termed the Composition-Knowledge Dichotomy. CPP explicitly concretizes propositions relevant to questions, enhancing reasoning performance especially in medical benchmarks requiring precise knowledge, while remaining competitive on math benchmarks focused on deductive reasoning. Experiments show CPP scales across various foundation models and parameter sizes, bridging the gap between composition- and knowledge-based approaches. This approach provides a foundation for logically organized and factually grounded reasoning, potentially improving the reliability of large language models in diverse applications.

item.title: Researchers present a harness-engineering approach for auditable enterprise LLM agents that enforces source boundaries, entity routing, and answer contracts with reproducible traces [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a harness-engineering method to transform prototype large language model (LLM) applications into auditable enterprise agents by moving deterministic behavior into code, manifests, schemas, and validation artifacts while maintaining source-backed claims as runtime authorities. They tested this approach on data from five Korean corporate groups, evaluating its ability to preserve source grounding, entity routing, traceability, output hygiene, and recommendation-language contracts under various validation scenarios and model substitutions. The study found that code-owned enforcement guarantees safety and utility better than prompt-based or external guardrail methods, offering a reusable pattern for developing traceable and controlled LLM applications with versioned source and validation artifacts.

item.title: Researchers present AegisDx, a safety-oriented AI framework for differential diagnosis that improves must-not-miss condition detection and diagnostic accuracy over standalone LLMs [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: AegisDx is a new AI framework designed to enhance clinical differential diagnosis by coordinating specialized large language model components with safety checks, evidence verification, and structured outputs. It aims to reduce diagnostic errors by explicitly screening for dangerous conditions and verifying reasoning against medical evidence. Evaluations on case reports from NEJM, JAMA, and emergency medicine datasets showed AegisDx improved Top-3 diagnostic accuracy and captured must-not-miss diagnoses more effectively than standalone LLMs. A blinded physician review of emergency department notes also rated AegisDx higher on safety metrics compared to GPT-5. These results suggest that focusing on safety-oriented reasoning frameworks can provide more reliable and transparent AI decision support in acute care settings.

item.title: Researchers find agreement among large language models is a weak and regime-dependent predictor of correctness, with over-confidence in frontier models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study analyzing 265,000 samples from 53 model runs shows that agreement within and across large language models (LLMs) does not reliably indicate accuracy, as models can share biases or heuristics. Agreement is a positive but weak predictor of correctness, most useful for mid-tier models and compute allocation, but frontier models exhibit high agreement with frequent confident errors. The researchers publicly released the anonymized data to support further analysis.

item.title: Researchers find persuasion attacks can increase approval of harmful actions in chain-of-thought monitoring by 9.5%, propose model-diverse fact-checking to reduce violations by up to 45% [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers tested the vulnerability of chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring in AI agents to persuasion-based attacks, where adversarial agents use natural-language arguments to convince monitors to approve policy-violating actions. Their evaluation across 40 tasks showed that access to CoT reasoning actually increased harmful action approvals by 9.5% on average, as the reasoning traces provided an additional channel for persuasion. To mitigate this, the team introduced a fact-checking framework pairing monitors and fact-checkers from different model families, such as a Claude 3.7 Sonnet monitor with a GPT-4.1 fact-checker, which reduced approval of policy violations by up to 45%, compared to only 6% when both roles used the same model. The findings suggest that CoT monitoring alone may be insufficient against adversarial persuasion and that diverse model fact-checking offers a more robust safety mechanism.

item.title: Researchers propose PARA-PV, a physics-aware retrieval-augmented framework for photovoltaic power forecasting integrating frozen foundation models and distribution shift correction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce PARA-PV, a new framework for photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting that incorporates physical knowledge throughout the process to improve accuracy amid weather variability and regime-dependent dynamics. The method encodes PV observations into patch-level representations and retrieves historical analogs consistent with current conditions to generate a physically grounded base forecast, which is then calibrated using a frozen Chronos time-series foundation model and adjusted for distribution shifts caused by changing weather and diurnal regimes. The framework also employs a physics-constrained loss function that partitions data into operational regimes such as peak, ramping, and night-time, adaptively reweighting errors to enhance learning of critical states. This approach aims to address challenges in reliable grid dispatch and renewable energy integration by combining physical constraints with advanced machine learning techniques. The researchers have made their code publicly available for further development and validation.

item.title: Researchers introduce CausalDS, a benchmark for evaluating causal reasoning in data-science agents using synthetic structural causal models and realistic natural-language scenarios [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed CausalDS, a new benchmark designed to evaluate causal reasoning capabilities in data-science workflows powered by large language models. The benchmark features scenes generated from structural causal models with synthetic observational data and accompanying natural-language stories grounded in realistic domains, aiming to bridge the gap between symbolic causal reasoning and practical data analysis. CausalDS includes tasks spanning all three of Pearl's causal inference levels, with many requiring data science coding and tool use to handle imperfect observations. The benchmark also assesses models' ability to recognize when questions lack sufficient information to answer, treating abstention as a scored outcome. This approach jointly evaluates symbolic causal reasoning, uncertainty quantification, abstention, and tool use in integrated data-science agents.

item.title: Researchers present a neurosymbolic reasoning and learning method integrating answer set programming with energy-based models for end-to-end training in dynamic domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a general methodology combining answer set programming (ASP) with energy-based models to enable joint optimization in continuous latent spaces while incorporating background knowledge, constraints, and non-monotonic inference. The approach advances prior work at the intersection of answer sets, probabilistic logic, and answer set modulo theories by providing a robust, ASP-centric platform for end-to-end training applicable to dynamic tasks involving perception and interaction. The team implemented the method and demonstrated its use with the MNIST dataset, evaluating performance on the visual question-answering benchmark Clevr and the multi-object tracking benchmark MOT, illustrating its practical applicability in complex reasoning and learning scenarios.

item.title: Researchers introduce overthinking models that amplify reasoning weights to reveal hidden information in language models up to 10 times more frequently [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a method called overthinking that amplifies reasoning task vectors in language models to better extract hidden information during black box auditing. By combining parameters of non-reasoning and reasoning-distilled models with an amplification factor, they create overthinking models that enhance the propensity to think out loud and surface secrets or unintended behaviors acquired during training. The study introduces layer-wise attenuation strategies to selectively amplify reasoning without degrading output quality and coherence. Experiments across models ranging from 2 billion to 32 billion parameters demonstrate that overthinking models reveal hidden information more effectively across multiple settings. The way secrets surface varies by type, with some requiring perturbation along the reasoning direction and others responding to any sufficiently large weight perturbation.

item.title: Researchers propose ASMR, an agentic AI framework to automatically generate compact schemas from historical ship maintenance reports using multi-granularity clustering and reinforcement learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce ASMR, a modular AI system designed to automatically create informative schemas from diverse historical ship maintenance and operational reports. The framework includes a Field Generation Agent that extracts semantic concepts and generates candidate schema fields, and a Structural Optimizer Agent that uses reinforcement learning to produce compact, non-redundant schema representations. Preliminary results suggest ASMR can help authors produce more complete and consistent reports, while highlighting challenges at the intersection of data management, agentic AI, and human-centered AI.

item.title: Researchers propose a first-principles mathematical theory of slow thinking and active perception, introducing 'active lifting' to model cognitive functions and large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This paper presents a mathematical framework for modeling slow thinking and active perception, focusing on the design, training, and inference of slow thinking large language models. The authors introduce a theory called "active lifting," which involves sampling latent sequences and an intrinsic drive to reduce uncertainty, leading to a broad design space that includes slow thinking models within a static theory subspace. The theory also derives an inference process with an internal time axis and a training objective resembling minimum-length coding and language invention, characterizing perception agency and slow thinking emergence. Key technical contributions include a three-stage pathway for improving slow thinking models, a unified method for constructing encoders and generative models across data modalities, a priori formation of human-like visual representations, and a potential solution to policy collapse. The work aims to provide foundational insights into cognitive modeling and the development of advanced AI systems.

item.title: Researchers introduce ZendoWorld, an interactive environment to test AI agents on visual concept induction and active hypothesis testing [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: ZendoWorld is a controlled interactive environment designed to challenge AI agents to infer logical rules from visual observations, propose new scenes to gather information, and refine hypotheses based on feedback. The study evaluates various agent types, including vision-language model reasoning, Bayesian filtering, dynamic concept discovery, and neuro-symbolic methods, revealing that high label prediction accuracy does not guarantee rule recovery and that different agents face distinct perception and induction challenges. Human data collected on the task shows a gap in inductive reasoning for complex rules, highlighting areas for improvement in AI, especially for applications like scientific discovery.

item.title: Researchers introduce AutoPersonas, a multi-timescale loop engine designed to reduce self-locking in long-term AI persona evolution by separating environment occurrences, observations, and persona state [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers identify self-locking as a failure mode in long-term AI persona agents, where generated behaviors become repetitive and stagnant. They propose AutoPersonas, an engine that separates environment occurrences, observations, and persona state to enable controlled divergence and evidence-based adaptation, aiming to preserve identity while allowing evolution. A three-year compressed simulation and a 40-day stress test with eight models revealed high repetition rates and weak relationship persistence, but techniques like context-slice masking and divergence targeting reduced thematic repetition and increased diversity. A fictional-world test confirmed the approach's ability to prevent fixation without real-world data intrusions. These findings suggest that separating controlled divergence from evidence-governed absorption can mitigate self-locking in AI personas, supporting more dynamic and continuous persona evolution while maintaining identity continuity.

item.title: Researchers introduce a compete-then-collaborate framework where four AI teachers build a verifiable curriculum to improve a coding student beyond imitation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers present a framework where four leading AI models-Claude, Codex-GPT, Grok, and Gemini-are ranked by an execution-based judge and then collaborate to create a verifiable curriculum for training a coding student model, Qwen2.5-Coder. They find that while all teachers perform well on standard problems, harder tasks differentiate their abilities, but student improvement does not depend on teacher ranking. Imitation learning on verified solutions can degrade student performance, whereas reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards improves it significantly. The study highlights that AI teacher collaboration is more effective when focused on constructing a verifiable learning environment rather than pooling answers for imitation. The team also releases a reproducible on-premises pipeline for further research.

item.title: Researchers introduce MentalHospital, a virtual environment for evaluating LLM-based psychiatric clinical encounters using 1,193 de-identified EHR cases across 76 disorders [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: MentalHospital simulates the full psychiatric clinical workflow including interviewing, examination, diagnosis, and treatment planning, assessed through objective EHR comparisons and subjective clinical quality evaluations. The system incorporates MentalEval, five domain-specific evaluators trained with expert guidance to measure communication, professionalism, note quality, diagnostic rigor, and treatment appropriateness. Surveyed clinicians rated MentalHospital's clinical fidelity at 3.88 out of 5, and MentalEval showed strong alignment with expert judgments. Benchmarking revealed that even the best large language models lag behind clinicians by over 37 percentage points in psychiatric competence, with mental status assessment identified as a major challenge.

item.title: Researchers distill an 8B reasoning model into a 0.6B on-device student for structured text enrichment, achieving faster processing and partial quality recovery [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers distilled an 8-billion-parameter reasoning teacher model into a 0.6-billion-parameter student model for on-device structured text enrichment, mapping news articles to JSON objects with summaries and labels. The student runs significantly faster, processing articles in about 0.8 seconds compared to the teacher's 39 seconds, and recovers 58% of the quality gap in summaries, outperforming baseline methods like constrained decoding and few-shot prompting. The study included controls with a same-size non-reasoning teacher and a larger managed pipeline, evaluated by a blinded panel against full articles. The results show that the reasoning teacher transfers writing quality, while the managed pipeline improves label diversity, and the non-reasoning teacher does not improve student performance beyond the untuned base. Some students trained on reasoning teachers fabricated content more often on short, thin-source articles, indicating a trade-off between writing quality and factual grounding. Because no single model excels in all aspects, the researchers propose a per-field routing map to optimize on-device text enrichment tasks.

item.title: PolyUQuest launches verifiable, structure-aware web retrieval-augmented generation using heterogeneous graphs, improving accuracy and efficiency on Hong Kong Polytechnic University websites [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: PolyUQuest is a new retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework that leverages a heterogeneous graph combining hyperlink topology, DOM hierarchy, and entity relations to preserve structural and semantic signals from web pages. It uses a two-tier router to select among three retrieval modes tailored to query needs, enabling verifiable answers with traceable sources. Evaluated on over 4,000 pages and tens of thousands of entities from Hong Kong Polytechnic University's official websites, PolyUQuest outperforms existing RAG systems in correctness, coverage, and faithfulness while reducing language model token usage per query. The system includes an interactive interface for inspecting answers and retrieval paths and is planned for deployment as a student-facing question-answering service at PolyU.

item.title: Researchers propose PredicateLongBench to systematically evaluate long-context reasoning in large language models across multiple difficulty axes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce PredicateLongBench, a benchmark designed to test large language models' long-context reasoning by identifying the longest contiguous subsequence of words satisfying specific predicates in long inputs. The benchmark includes synthetic and real-world data generation pipelines and explores various difficulty axes to assess multiple aspects of long-context understanding. Initial results show that leading models struggle as task difficulty increases, highlighting current limitations in long-context capabilities despite the tasks' conceptual simplicity and lack of reliance on model-generated content or judges.

item.title: Researchers propose psychological competence as a new dimension for evaluating human-facing AI systems, focusing on user cognition, emotional interpretation, and decision-making support [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Current AI evaluation frameworks emphasize technical metrics like accuracy and robustness but often overlook the psychological impact of AI systems that interact directly with users through natural language. This paper introduces psychological competence as the ability of AI to appropriately support user cognition, emotional understanding, and behavior in context, highlighting factors such as tone, authority, and responsiveness. The authors outline a conceptual framework for assessing psychological competence using scenario-based probes, structured human evaluations, and model-assisted methods. They argue that this dimension should be integrated into AI evaluation by developers, deployers, researchers, and regulators to better address the real-world effects of AI systems acting as advisors, coaches, tutors, or companions.

item.title: Researchers propose INTENT, an LSTM-based framework predicting vehicle intentions at intersections with 99.71% accuracy on the InD dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: The INTENT framework uses a long short-term memory (LSTM) model to predict vehicle intentions-going straight, turning left, or turning right-at intersections two seconds before the event occurs. This approach aims to improve autonomous vehicle safety and agility by enabling better interpretation of driver intentions in complex scenarios such as intersections, roundabouts, and emergency stops. The model was extensively tested with ablation studies on the InD dataset, achieving 99.71% accuracy. Vehicle intention prediction is critical for timely evasive actions and can also enhance trajectory prediction by conditioning on predicted intentions.

item.title: Researchers introduce Blind-Spots-Bench to evaluate persistent weaknesses in multimodal AI models using 235 human-simple tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Blind-Spots-Bench, a new benchmark designed to reveal persistent blind spots in modern multimodal AI models by testing them on tasks that are simple for humans but challenging for AI. The benchmark includes 235 samples derived from student questions, annotated with structured reference solutions, and covers language, vision-language, and image-generation models. An automated grading pipeline was created to evaluate both open-weight and closed-source models, revealing that closed-source frontier models outperform open-weight ones by about 10% despite similar performance on existing benchmarks. The analysis also found no single model excels across all task types, highlighting ongoing challenges and the benchmark's value as a diagnostic tool for identifying specific AI weaknesses.

item.title: Researchers introduce MobiDiff, a discrete diffusion framework for generating synthetic human mobility data with semantic multi-channel modeling, showing improved speed and fidelity over prior methods [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed MobiDiff, an end-to-end discrete diffusion model that generates synthetic human mobility data by directly denoising multi-channel semantic skeletons representing spatial, activity, and temporal information. This approach avoids complex interpolation and latent trace construction used in previous diffusion-based methods, enabling efficient and interpretable modeling of discrete semantic events in mobility data. MobiDiff was evaluated on large-scale datasets from Atlanta, Boston, and Seattle, demonstrating competitive preservation of trajectory lengths and temporal intervals while being 5.3 times faster on average than the state-of-the-art GeoGen method during inference. The results suggest that discrete diffusion offers a promising framework for privacy-preserving and efficient synthetic mobility data generation useful for transportation optimization and urban planning.

item.title: FedOPAL introduces one-shot federated learning with analytic visual prompt tuning to improve feature alignment and reduce server-side costs in edge intelligence [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: FedOPAL is a new federated learning framework designed to address communication bandwidth bottlenecks and computational costs in edge intelligence. It uses visual prompts as feature rectifiers to correct heterogeneous data distributions, enabling efficient gradient-free aggregation with least-squares closed-form solutions while maintaining accuracy comparable to iterative methods. The framework overcomes limitations of existing analytical federated learning approaches that assume static features, which fail under non-independent and identically distributed data. Experimental results demonstrate that FedOPAL significantly outperforms original analytical methods on multiple benchmarks and eliminates server-side training costs, offering a scalable solution for collaborative learning with large models on edge devices.

item.title: Researchers identify knowledge-circuit misalignment as cause of generalization failures in fine-tuned large language models, proposing self-patching to improve reasoning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers studied why large language models (LLMs) quickly memorize new facts during fine-tuning but fail to apply them in downstream reasoning tasks, defining this as the Knowing--Using Gap. They introduced self-patching, a technique that locates internal activations where relocating representations improves generalization failures, supporting a hypothesis that memorized knowledge is not routed to computation-effective layers. Their heuristic strategy recovers 58-75% of potential improvement in generalization, with experiments confirming robustness across domains.

item.title: Researchers develop G-Frame multi-agent framework to reduce hallucinations in lightweight language models, achieving 79% fewer errors and GPT-4o mini parity in chemistry tasks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce G-Frame, an adaptive multi-agent framework combining Bayesian and game theory principles to improve reasoning in lightweight language models used in scientific domains. By synthesizing a large specialized dataset and enforcing domain constraints, their 7-billion-parameter model OmniChem matches GPT-4o mini performance on chemistry benchmarks while reducing hallucinations by 79%. The model also demonstrates advanced capabilities in molecular design and synthesis planning. This approach offers a scalable method to enhance reasoning and accelerate knowledge discovery in specialized scientific fields.

item.title: OmniFood-Bench evaluates vision-language models on nutrient reasoning and personalized health advice using MM-Food-100K dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce OmniFood-Bench, a benchmark designed to assess vision-language models (VLMs) on their ability to perform nutrient reasoning and provide personalized dietary advice. The benchmark tests models across three levels: basic perception of ingredients and cooking methods, quantitative reasoning for portion size and nutritional profiling, and safety-critical recommendations for disease-specific diets. Six state-of-the-art VLMs, including gpt-5.1, gemini-3-flash, and qwen3-vl-8B, were evaluated, revealing that while models can accurately identify dishes, they struggle with estimating mass and often generate incorrect advice for high-risk diabetic patients. This work highlights challenges in deploying autonomous agents for public health and sets a standard for evaluating their trustworthiness.

item.title: Researchers apply JEPA-style predictive learning to JA4-derived network fingerprints using a Transformer model trained on 397K samples from JA4DB and CIC-IDS-2017 [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers developed JA4-JEPA, a Transformer-based model trained on JA4, JA4H, JA4S, and JA4X subfields from JA4DB and CIC-IDS-2017 datasets, totaling approximately 397,000 samples. The model uses JEPA-style predictive learning, which matches latent predictions to target encoder outputs instead of regenerating inputs, a method previously successful in images and video. The learned representations were evaluated with a frozen k-nearest neighbors probe on protocol-family classification tasks across TLS, DNS, and SSH protocols. On 39,416 heldout samples, the model achieved a cosine similarity of 0.9899 and a kNN accuracy of 0.9220, indicating that JEPA-style learning can produce effective embeddings from JA4-derived network fingerprints even when view overlap across sources is incomplete.

item.title: Researchers introduce Drift-Aware Temporal Graph Rewiring (DATGR) to model semantic evolution in biomedical text, improving link prediction on BIOMRC dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Biomedical language changes rapidly with new discoveries, causing traditional static text models to lose accuracy over time. Researchers propose Drift-Aware Temporal Graph Rewiring (DATGR), a framework that dynamically updates co-occurrence graph edges based on estimated semantic drift without retraining embeddings for each time slice. Evaluated on the Biomedical Multi-Relation Corpus (BIOMRC), DATGR improved mean AUROC by 0.066 over a static baseline while maintaining comparable precision-recall performance, demonstrating effective and efficient adaptation to temporal semantic changes in biomedical text.

item.title: Researchers use AI models to identify and generate facial stimuli that optimize detection of emotion perception differences between autistic and neurotypical adults [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers developed population-specific neural network models to predict facial emotion judgments in autistic and neurotypical adults, identifying a small subset of diagnostic expressions that highlight group differences. They used these models to select novel faces that maximized behavioral differences and applied generative adversarial networks to transform images toward greater group agreement, reducing behavioral separation in validation tests. This model-guided approach offers a framework for creating optimized behavioral assays that reveal nuanced perceptual differences and improve phenotyping beyond fixed stimulus sets.

item.title: CommuniWave:A Machine Learning Model for Quantifying the Degree of Temporary Informal Behavior in Urban Communities [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For urban managers and designers, improving the functional attributes of urban communities to enhance territorial resilience in the face of complexity and uncertainty is crucial. Currently, community planning often follows a top-down approach and lacks effective metrics to quantify informal behaviors of residents, leading to frequent conflicts with original plans. This study introduces CommuniWave, a machine learning model designed to efficiently detect and quantify the Degree of Informal Behavior (DIB) in urban communities. The model integrates a Behavior Capture Net (BCN) based on mmaction2, a self-developed YOLOv10 model (YLX), and a Behavior Eval Model (BEM) using random forest. Ultimately, by generating DIB fluctuation charts from street videos, the model facilitates dynamic monitoring, supporting urban managers in making refined decisions to enhance the overall resilience of communities.

item.title: SHAP-Weighted Cross-Modal Expert Fusion for Emotion and Sentiment Recognition: Evidence and Limits [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal emotion and sentiment recognition is commonly addressed by early fusion, which concatenates modalities before classification, or late fusion, which combines independently trained unimodal predictors. Early fusion can be accurate but monolithic, while late fusion is modular but may lose cross-modal interactions. This paper revisits XAI-guided adaptive fusion (\xgaf), a tree-based mixture of unimodal and cross-modal experts whose sample-level weights are derived from TreeSHAP attribution magnitudes. We focus on the effect of SHAP attribution reduction when experts have unequal feature dimensionalities. In this setting, mean-abs and median-abs reductions can suppress high-dimensional cross-modal experts, whereas sum-abs reduction preserves total attribution mass. On MELD 7-class emotion recognition, sum-abs \xgaf{} nearly matches early fusion across three face-sequence aggregators; the Transformer variant reaches 0.5983 \wf{}, compared with 0.6018 for early fusion and 0.4598 for probability-average late fusion. McNemar testing shows no significant difference between sum-abs \xgaf{} and early fusion on MELD ($p=1.000$), while \xgaf{} remains significantly better than late fusion ($p<0.0001$). On CMU-MOSEI 3-class sentiment recognition, sum-abs \xgaf{} reaches 0.6519 \wf{}, slightly exceeding early fusion (0.6485) and late fusion (0.5696). Ablation studies show that the main gain comes from adding cross-modal experts, especially the trimodal expert, rather than from complex per-sample routing. Diagnostics further show that mean-abs and median-abs weights are nearly uniform, while sum-abs weights concentrate on the trimodal expert. Thus, the main contribution is a transparent empirical analysis of how SHAP reduction, expert dimensionality, and cross-modal expert design affect modular multimodal fusion.

item.title: Towards Precision Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Clinical-Reasoning LLM for Risk Stratification and Treatment Guidance [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a common malignancy and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality. Current guidelines and staging systems provide coarse categories, but often miss within-stage heterogeneity and the clinical context in electronic medical records (EMRs). We present HCC-STAR (Hepatocellular Carcinoma Staging, Treatment And pRognosis), a clinically aligned large language model that reads routine EMR narratives and jointly outputs risk score-based staging, ranked guideline-consistent treatments with evidence-based rationales, and individualized survival estimates. We curated about 30,000 HCC cases from SEER and expanded them into EMR-style narrative training data using a clinician-validated, prompt-based augmentation workflow. On this corpus, we developed a knowledge-aligned reasoning framework optimized with a step-verifiable composite reward, moving beyond text-level memorization of clinical guidelines. In a multi-center cohort of 6,668 patients from 12 hospitals in China, HCC-STAR achieved state-of-the-art performance in treatment recommendation and risk stratification compared with clinical guidelines and competitive models, including GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5 Pro. Hypothetical overall-survival analysis showed a median survival of 51 months under adherence to HCC-STAR recommendations, compared with 29 and 32 months under BCLC and CNLC. In clinician-centric evaluations, blinded hepatobiliary specialists rated HCC-STAR's reasoning and evidence-based justifications as trustworthy. The model surpassed resident and attending physicians in treatment accuracy and helped physicians make more accurate decisions faster when used as an assistant. These findings support HCC-STAR as a reliable and verifiable decision-support system for risk stratification and precision therapy in HCC.

item.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08625v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Consumer-facing health chatbots powered by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for symptom assessment. However, chatbot development and evaluation often rely on cooperative, articulate, simulated patients. We analysed 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations and found that communication patterns and expression of emotions vary widely across users. We developed a patient simulator that separately models clinical content, emotional state, conversational strategy, and communication style. In a Turing-inspired evaluation of realism with 15 human graders, simulated conversations were nearly indistinguishable from real ones, with human graders achieving an accuracy of 55%. We used five distinct patient personae, across 1,164 clinician-graded cases, to evaluate the performance of four LLMs in urgency assessment. We found that communication style can significantly alter triage outcomes. Patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence must accommodate communication diversity: systems designed for idealised, rather than realistic, interactions risk underperforming and amplifying health disparities when deployed in the real world.

item.title: Formal Mechanisms for Market Stability in Self-Interested Agent Societies: A Marketplace Simulation Study [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08652v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-interested agents, left unconstrained, tend toward defection in repeated social dilemmas, causing cooperative gains from trade to collapse. This paper investigates what formal mechanisms, layered on top of unrestricted communication, are sufficient for a society of such agents to maintain market stability, and how resilient those mechanisms are to adversarial attack. We instantiate the research question as a multi-agent marketplace simulation where 18 LLM agents (DeepSeek-V3) with complementary production specialties must trade within a constrained social network to obtain utility. We conduct two experimental phases: (1) a mechanism comparison across eight conditions under progressive troll injection over 200 rounds, identifying Mediation as the top-performing mechanism; and (2) adversarial red-teaming of Mediation using iteratively prompt-optimised LLM-driven trolls, finding that the best attack (v6) reduces honest-agent utility by 13.3% but cannot collapse the market. Mediation enables recovery even under sustained adversarial pressure. We define adversarial robustness as a mechanism's ability to sustain positive honest-agent utility under optimised attack, and find that Mediation is robust: it can be bent but not broken.

item.title: SolarChain-Eval: A Physics-Constrained Benchmark for Trustworthy Economic Agents in Decentralized Energy Markets [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As agentic AI systems are increasingly applied to cyber-physical environments, their evaluation requires assessment of both task performance and trustworthiness. In decentralized energy markets, autonomous agents may improve market utility, but may also exploit invalid physical data, create artificial liquidity, and produce unstable governance decisions. Therefore, we propose SolarChain-Eval, a physics-constrained benchmark for evaluating trustworthy economic agents. It formulates market governance as a Gymnasium-compatible Markov Decision Process, where agents make hourly decisions. SolarChain-Eval evaluates each policy across multiple dimensions, including market utility, physical safety, slippage, action smoothness, spatial fairness, and auditability. To support agentic evaluation, SolarChain-Eval incorporates an LLM-based Planner/Auditor layer. The Planner defines episode-level action bounds and audit rules, while the Auditor reviews and revises high-risk actions. All interventions are recorded through structured logs, including trigger signals, proposed actions, revised actions, and audit rationales. Experiments with static, random, myopic, RL, and RL+LLM policies reveal a clear utility-safety trade-off. RL agents improve market utility but can still produce unsafe behavior. When the physics penalty is removed, reward-maximizing agents exploit invalid generation and increase artificial liquidity. The LLM Planner/Auditor improves auditability and mitigates selected risks, but it cannot fully compensate for a misspecified reward function. These results indicate that trustworthy agentic AI evaluation requires both physical constraints and transparent intervention traces. We release data and code as open access on GitHub for replicability.

item.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08716v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In long-horizon tasks, decision-relevant state is often scattered across an expanding trajectory, while the action agent must surface it and act. As trajectories grow, task requirements, environment facts, prior attempts, diagnoses, and open subgoals can be buried in the context window or pushed beyond it, failing to influence decisions when needed. We call this failure mode "behavioral state decay". We study memory as an active intervention mechanism rather than passive retrieval. A separate memory agent runs alongside an unmodified action agent, updating a structured memory bank from the recent trajectory and deciding whether to inject a memory-grounded reminder or remain silent. The module is plug-and-play with frontier action agents and existing agent harnesses. Across Terminal-Bench 2.0 and $\tau^2$-Bench, it improves pass@1 for both weaker and stronger action agents, with gains of +8.3 pp on Terminal-Bench and +6.8 pp on $\tau^2$-Bench. Ablations show that selective intervention outperforms passive bank exposure, always-on injection, advisor-only guidance, and general retrieval. As an early step toward open-weight memory policies, we train Qwen3.5-27B on SETA using SFT and GRPO, improving validation reward and achieving partial transfer to Terminal-Bench.

item.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Post-training quantization is widely used to deploy large language models in resource-constrained settings, yet its evaluation relies almost exclusively on accuracy and perplexity. We show that these metrics fail to capture behavioral changes induced by quantization. We introduce correctness agreement, a decision-level metric that measures overlap in correct predictions between a base model and its quantized variants, independent of absolute accuracy. Across multiple models and quantization schemes from 8-bit to 2-bit, we find that behavioral divergence emerges under moderate quantization even when task performance appears preserved. To explain this effect, we analyze quantization as a structural operator on attention weights and quantify layer-wise distortions using statistical and distributional measures. Our results reveal non-linear breakpoints at low bit-widths and show that query and key projections are consistently more sensitive than value and output projections. These findings expose an illusion of equivalence between base and quantized models and motivate behavioral evaluation beyond conventional performance metrics.

item.title: Workflow as Knowledge: Semantic Persistence for LLM-Mediated Workflows [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) applications increasingly use explicit workflows for tool use, retrieval, branching, checkpointing, and human approval. Existing workflow systems already address many execution concerns. This paper proposes a Lisp-inspired but language-independent conceptual model: symbolic forms, object identity, and live-image thinking are used as explanatory lenses, not implementation commitments. In this model, workflow definitions, workflow instances, inference records, context snapshots, and dependency relations are represented as persistent knowledge objects in a shared knowledge substrate. Its central semantic distinction is between derive and infer: derive is deterministic computation over available state; infer is mediated LLM judgment under declared context and executor-controlled capability policy. The result is a preliminary conceptual account of semantic persistence: workflows do not merely produce knowledge and leave traces, but can themselves be represented as inspectable, resumable, and reviewable knowledge objects, while formal transition semantics remain future work.

item.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in Vision-Language Models, Large Language Models, and Multimodal Large Language Models have improved autonomous driving tasks such as scene understanding, decision making, trajectory prediction, and visual question answering. However, evaluating whether these models can reliably reason about safety-critical incidents remains challenging. To address this gap, we present AUTOPILOT-VQA, an incident-centric visual question answering benchmark for dashcam video understanding. The dataset evaluates different systems through structured questions designed around real-world driving incidents and near-incidents. The benchmark covers diverse safety-relevant categories, including weather and lighting conditions, traffic environment, road layout, road surface state, signage, involved entities, accident occurrence, impact location, and avoidability-related reasoning. By requiring models to answer grounded questions about both contextual scene properties and event-level incident details, AUTOPILOT-VQA moves beyond object recognition toward temporally grounded, safety-aware reasoning. The dataset is released as part of the AUTOPILOT CVPR 2026 competition and provides a standardized benchmark for assessing the reliability of autonomous driving systems in different scenarios. Our benchmark support developments for more interpretable, robust, and safety-conscious vision-language systems for real-world autonomous driving.

item.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this study, we present a large-scale descriptive analysis of the use of an AI-based learning assistant (Syntea) in higher education. Based on objective log data from 77,543 students enrolled in distance studies, we examine usage patterns across gender, age group, study cluster, degree, and study mode. To date, existing research on educational chatbots has largely relied on comparatively small samples and self-reported survey data, while large-scale evidence on actual usage behavior remains limited. Our findings show that Syntea is already embedded in the study routines of many learners, but that usage differs across demographic and structural contexts. By identifying these patterns, our study provides an empirical basis for the further development of AI-based learning support and contributes a large-scale analysis of educational chatbot usage in higher education.

item.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.08758v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific ideas rarely start from a blank page. They inherit mechanisms, repair known limitations, and recombine pieces of earlier work, much like biological genomes. Current benchmarks still say little about whether AI systems can follow this inheritance structure. We present IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a benchmark for scientific lineage reasoning and lineage-grounded idea generation. IG-Bench is organized around the IdeaGene framework: each paper or proposal is represented as a set of minimal, typed, evidence-grounded Idea Genome objects, and a GenomeDiff aligns these objects to record inheritance, mutation, loss, external import, and novel insertion under six operational evolutionary dynamics. The benchmark contains 1,961 golden lineage traces, 1,085 curated Idea Genome objects, and 920 pairwise GenomeDiff records across 10 scientific domains. It supports two evaluations. IG-Exam (42 task types, 1,029 instances) tests closed-form lineage reasoning across Idea Genome abstraction, inheritance tracing, evolutionary reasoning, and lineage verification. IG-Arena evaluates generation with a lineage-conditioned Population-Evolution Score(PES), asking whether a proposal can be inserted as a coherent descendant of a given lineage population: it should inherit the right Idea Genome objects, vary meaningfully from nearby work, and offer selection value for future research. Experiments on 14 LLM-based scientists expose a compositional bottleneck. The strongest system reaches only 27.3% exact accuracy on lineage reasoning, and structured lineage context reshuffles system rankings rather than helping every participant uniformly.

item.title: Towards the Explainability of Temporal Graph Networks via Memory Backtracking and Topological Attribution [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07716v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Temporal graphs are ubiquitous in real-world applications and Temporal Graph Networks (TGNs) have achieved superior predictive accuracy. Understanding which historical events drive model predictions can enhance trustworthiness of TGNs. Existing explanation methods overlook the memory module, the core component that records and updates node histories, leaving the influence of past events unexplored. To address this, we attribute TGNs predictions through the topology attribution tree and memory backtracking tree. The topology attribution tree captures the influence of neighbors and their memory vectors, then the memory backtracking tree quantifies how historical events shape node memory vectors. We apply the LRP in TGNs, ensuring that the total contribution of events equals the logits of model. Finally, top-k selection may be unfaithful due to the nonlinear mapping from logits to probabilities, we design optimization objectives to identify the important events. Experiments on nine temporal graph datasets, spanning node property prediction, link prediction tasks and graph classification tasks, show that our method provides faithful explanations and outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/yazhengliu/MemExplainer

item.title: LLT: Local Linear Transformer for PDE Operator Learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07718v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural operators have become a common approach for learning PDE solution maps and accelerating numerical simulations. Transformer-based neural operators are of particular interest, since attention can learn long-range dependencies in the computational domain. However, standard attention has two major limitations when applied to PDEs: it scales quadratically with the number of computational nodes, and it lacks an explicit bias toward local interactions. To address these issues, we introduce Local Linear Transformer (LLT) for PDE operator learning. The architecture combines linear global attention with local spatial mixing, and incorporates coordinate and geometry information. We evaluate LLT on several PDE problems, including elasticity, plasticity, airfoil flow, pipe flow, and Darcy flow. The reference data for these problems span finite-element, finite-volume, and finite-difference discretizations on structured and unstructured meshes. Compared with other neural-operator and transformer baselines from prior studies, LLT achieves competitive or lower relative $L_2$ error across these problems. On matched structured discretizations, wall-clock time per training iteration is reduced by factors of 1.8 to 2.5 relative to Transolver. We also scale the approach and apply it to a three-dimensional car aerodynamics dataset with 32,186 unstructured mesh points per sample. Together, these results indicate that LLT provides an accurate and computationally efficient operator for PDE problems across discretizations, mesh types, and problem settings.

item.title: ReCoLoRA: Spectrum-Aware Recursive Consolidation for Continual LLM Fine-Tuning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07719v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning adapts a large language model to one task cheaply, but across a task sequence LoRA-style methods keep stacking low-rank updates on the same frozen weight, so each new task tends to overwrite the previous ones. We present ReCoLoRA (Recursive Consolidation of Low-Rank Adapters), a spectrum-aware framework for continual fine-tuning: adapters are initialized from a randomized SVD of the pretrained weight, per-layer effective ranks are selected by an elbow criterion, and the principal subspace is adapted before residual capacity is opened. Before each new task, ReCoLoRA re-decomposes the current effective weight, rather than the original one, into a frozen residual, a slowly updated principal component, and a fresh adapter (recursive consolidation), so every task starts from the model that has already absorbed its predecessors. On a six-task continual GLUE sequence over four 7-8B backbones, ReCoLoRA attains the best final average score on three of the four backbones against rank-swept LoRA, PiSSA, AdaLoRA, and DoRA baselines while training fewer parameters; an oracle-routed task-bank variant serves as an upper bound under full task isolation. Code: https://github.com/bhqy666/ReCoLoRA.

item.title: Omni-Sleep: A Sleep Foundation Model via Hierarchical Contrastive Learning of CNS--ANS Dynamic [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07720v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sleep physiology arises from the coordinated dynamics of the central nervous system (CNS) and autonomic nervous system (ANS), as reflected by multimodal polysomnography signals including EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, and respiration. However, existing sleep foundation models often fuse heterogeneous biosignals in a topology-agnostic manner, overlooking their physiological organization. We introduce Omni-Sleep, a sleep foundation model that uses the CNS/ANS partition as a physiological prior for topology-constrained representation learning. Omni-Sleep learns structured representations through three objectives: intra-system consistency, which captures shared subsystem-level factors within neural and cardio-respiratory signals; inter-system synchronization, which aligns subsystem trajectories to model brain--body dynamics; and latent-space masked temporal modeling, which captures long-horizon sleep dynamics. Pre-trained on over 100,000 hours of multi-center multimodal PSG data, Omni-Sleep is evaluated on sleep staging and multi-disease classification. Across datasets and modality-ablation settings, Omni-Sleep outperforms strong foundation-model baselines, showing improved label efficiency, cross-dataset generalization, and robustness to missing modalities. These results highlight the value of physiological hierarchy for generalizable sleep representation learning. Code is available at https://github.com/AutoBrain-sleep/OmniSleep.

item.title: SHIFT: Survival Prediction from Incomplete and Heterogeneous Genomic Data [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07725v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Genomic prediction models often fail to transfer across institutions because sequencing panels differ across sites, creating structural feature missingness at deployment. Existing approaches to this challenge typically restrict analysis to genes shared across cohorts, exclude patients with incomplete profiles, or rely on test-time imputation, all of which can reduce robustness and limit the use of multi-center data. We propose Survival prediction Handling Incomplete Features using Transformer (SHIFT), a missingness-aware survival model that directly predicts from incomplete genomic inputs without test-time imputation. SHIFT represents each genomic feature separately and uses masked self-attention, along with a feature-availability mask, so that predictions are based only on observed inputs. Further, we introduce variable-rate feature masking during training to improve robustness to heterogeneous missingness patterns. We evaluate the approach on glioblastoma and lung squamous cell carcinoma with external validation across multiple cohorts, including a challenging setting with severe cross-cohort panel mismatch. Across these settings, SHIFT shows strong generalization and compares favorably with standard survival baselines and imputation-based approaches, while using a single model across differing feature sets. We also find that incorporating patients from incomplete cohorts during development can improve performance on external data, suggesting that partially observed cohorts need not be excluded from model building. These results support missingness-aware modeling as a practical strategy for multi-center survival prediction in precision oncology.

item.title: Collective Intelligence with Foundation Models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07729v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As foundation models grow in scale and diversity, coordinating multiple models into cooperative reasoning systems offers a path toward safer, more reliable AI. This chapter presents a multi-agent framework where solver models generate independent drafts, each undergoes structured critique and revision by a critic agent, and an aggregator agent synthesizes a final consensus solution. A scoring module provides semantic, numerical, and procedural evaluation across all agents. Through ablation studies on a benchmark spanning calculus, physics, chemistry, biology, economics, optimization, statistics, and mathematics, we isolate the contributions of framework architecture versus model diversity. We compare four configurations: (1) Individual Baseline, (2) Homogeneous Framework using one shared model, (3) Redundant Homogeneous Solvers using multiple instances of the same model, and (4) Heterogeneous Framework with diverse specialized models. Results show that while framework structure and redundant sampling yield modest gains, model heterogeneity is the critical factor driving substantial performance improvements. The heterogeneous configuration achieves superior step-wise accuracy (0.64 vs. 0.54 for individual models; 2.3x improvement over homogeneous configurations) with reduced variance across categories and difficulty levels. Step-wise reasoning quality (correctness of intermediate steps, not just final answers) improves dramatically only with model diversity, showing that heterogeneous agents provide complementary error detection and reasoning refinement essential for explainability and auditability. We discuss architectural principles, evaluation methodology, and implications for Global Applied AI, showing how heterogeneous multi-agent coordination supports transparent, auditable, high-confidence decision-making across scientific and industrial domains.

item.title: Jet-Long: Efficient Long-Context Extension with Dynamic Bifocal RoPE [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07740v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern LLMs are increasingly deployed in long-context applications such as retrieval-augmented generation, repository-level coding, and agentic workflows whose accumulated reasoning and tool traces routinely push the input an order of magnitude past the pretraining window, making zero-shot context extension the dominant deployment path for open-weight checkpoints. Most existing zero-shot methods fix a single rescaling factor up front, so an aggressive factor sacrifices short-context fidelity while a conservative one breaks down at long contexts. We propose Jet-Long, a tuning-free zero-shot method that pairs a local RoPE-faithful window with a long-range window whose rescaling factor adapts dynamically to the current sequence length, recovering the base model exactly at short inputs while extrapolating cleanly at long ones. An inclusion-exclusion attention merge and an on-the-fly RoPE correction rotation make the bifocal construction essentially free at inference; fused into a single CuTe kernel, long-context prefill reaches up to $1.39\times$ FA2 throughput on H100 (approaching the Hopper-only FA4), and single-batch generation incurs $\le 4\%$ overhead at every length. On Qwen3-1.7B/4B/8B up to 128K context, Jet-Long leads RULER by $+4.79$/$+2.18$/$+2.03$~pp over the strongest baseline at 1.7B/4B/8B, achieves the best overall accuracy on HELMET-RAG (a benchmark identified by HELMET as the most efficient predictor of downstream long-context performance) and attains the lowest PG-19 perplexity. Jet-Long also generalizes to hybrid attention architectures such as Jet-Nemotron for further long-context improvement without retraining, and remains hyperparameter-resilient for ease of deployment.

item.title: Architecture Generalization with MetaNCA [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07743v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-organization is an emergent property of life, driven by the collective behavior of individual components acting on local information. Biological neurons, through local interactions transmitted through synapses, are able to learn efficiently and can adapt their connections over an organism's lifespan. Motivated by these desirable properties of adaptability and local interaction, neural cellular automata (NCA) models have been successful at learning morphogenesis solely through local update rules, demonstrating stability over many updates and robustness to perturbations. In this work, we introduce Meta Neural Cellular Automata (MetaNCA), a framework that learns local rules which self-organize the weights of artificial neural networks. A learned rule network iteratively updates the weights of a task network using only local interactions on the computation graph. We propose a novel Weight Transformer architecture for the local rule network, which uses linear attention to aggregate signals from neighboring weights and hidden states. Once trained, the rule network generates task networks of diverse architectures without backpropagation. We show that MetaNCA generates weights for feedforward MLPs, CNNs, and ResNets on MNIST and CIFAR-100, scaling to networks of 2 million parameters. We further show that MetaNCA generalizes to architectures not seen during meta-training, and that architectural diversity in the training phase strengthens this generalization.

item.title: A Transdiagnostic Space of Disorder Like Phenotypes in Reinforcement Learning Agents [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.07753v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modelling psychological disorders in artificial agents offers both a testbed for computational psychiatry and a lens on the failure modes of affective control.
